header.name: Advanced Digital Communication
header.description: This course will introduce students to the fundamental blocks that constitute a digital communication system. After the introduction students will learn about designing digital communication receivers in an optimal manner by considering both noise and channel. Student will then study the digital modulation schemes and analyze their trade-off between bandwidth, power and spectral efficiency. This course will also cover important pracxtical topics like equalization and synchronization. Finally, the fundamental limits on reliable data transmission will be briefly covered.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will understand the necessity of digital communication systems, their fundamental components and the fundamental limits on reliable data transmission.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to design optimal receivers for digital communications using statistical communication theory principles and equivalent signal sets.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: The student will be able to analyze the performance and trade-off of the digital modulation schemes by considering equivalent signal sets and geometry of decision regions.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: The student will be able to design various signal processing procedures in communication systems such as channel estimation, equalization, synchronization etc.

resources.title: Digital Communication: John G. Proakis, McGraw Hill, 4th Edition,2001.
